Dagster's product is great, but comparing it to MWAA is unfair. MWAA is a poor quality product - difficult to use, unstable, inflexible, and poorly-supported. A fairer comparison would be against Astronomer.

I haven't worked with Dagster, but I've heard that it's lighter weight and local development is delightful. Dagster natively isolates tasks in the DAG into separate Kubernetes pods, unlike Airflow's CeleryExecutor on Astro.

Dagster contributor: TaskFlow superficially looks like some of Dagster's APIs, but the experience is way different - TaskFlow is built on XCom, which isn't designed for data sizes larger than small, and using it loses Python dependency isolation between DAGs.

Dagster and Prefect won't ever have a hosted version on AWS/GCP consoles like Airflow does; large existing Airflow shops with big DE teams can't easily move to Dagster or Prefect, nor do they want to.

In my opinion, Dagster is hitting the right chord: they focus on the pain points in DX for Airflow, they have figured out how to do development branches, they focus on assets rather than tasks, and constantly improve the product.

For anyone who has spent significant time with data and ML pipelines, read posts about Dagster... The software itself has matured significantly in the last year as well - highly recommend taking a look at this if you're building new pipelines.
After playing around with this tool a bit in the past I can't seem to understand what it's trying to solve. It comes across as a side project that VCs happened to throw money at.

Dagster team member: goals were local development (seamless laptop-to-prod dev experience), managing complexity of hundreds of DAGs/thousands of tasks, and testability by separating business logic from environmental concerns (unlike Airflow's hardcoded operators).
I've been working with this stack (Dagster, dbt, DuckDB) for a few months and am super happy with how well everything plays together.
